title: Reference
description: Every kind, table, relation, stage and check of a product, generated from its schema and check rows.

title: Record
description: One record as `lathe show` answers it: its row, parts, children and links.

title: Use case
description: A use case as its readers read it: the Use case page reads it whole as a tree (its requirements, each with its tests and the steps that fulfill it, and its flows by interface, each with its steps path by path and its flow test) with the record the page is about; a capability's list reads each use case's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Product
description: A product as its page and the nav read it: its row and roles, its business outcomes with the capabilities serving each, its domains, its product kinds with their fields, its product relations, its open questions with what they are about, and its interfaces with the flows through each and the use cases with none, by capability; and every product as a space.

title: Pattern
description: A pattern as its readers read it: the Pattern page reads it whole (its settings in order, its rules by ID, each with its tests per following domain) with the record the page is about; a product's list reads each pattern's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Who follows it is Pattern following's. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Standard
description: A standard as its readers read it: the Standard page reads it whole (its rules by ID, each with the records that meet it and its tests) with the record the page is about; a product's list reads each standard's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Domain
description: A domain as its readers read it: the Domain page reads it whole (its capabilities in order, each with the outcomes it serves and its use cases; its terms; its domain services, each with its service and tests; its repositories, each with the aggregate it persists) with the record the page is about; a product's list reads each domain's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Specification
description: A specification as its readers read it: the Specification page reads it whole (the aggregates it reads, its predicate with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses, its test with the test data sets it starts from) with the record the page is about; a domain's list reads each specification's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Aggregate
description: One aggregate whole, as the Aggregate aggregate holds it: its row, its entities with their fields and the entities they hold, their data models, and its invariants with their tests.

title: Domain event
description: One domain event whole, as the Domain event aggregate holds it: its row, the fields it carries in order, and its event type.

title: Command
description: One command whole, as the Command aggregate holds it: its row with the events it raises, the specifications it checks and the domain services it calls, its handler, and its policies with the event each hears, their event handlers and tests.

title: Value object
description: A value object as its readers read it: the Value object page reads it whole (its fields in order, its constraints by ID each with its test and the test data sets it starts from, its value type with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses) with the record the page is about; a product's list reads each value object's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Read model
description: A read model as its readers read it: the Read model page reads it whole (its fields in order, what it reads, calls and is fed by, its queries by ID each with what it selects by and calls and its handler, its projection and its reader, each piece of code with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses) with the record the page is about; a domain's list reads each read model's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: View page
description: One view as its readers see it: its row and its view requirements, each with its tests; and the views of a product in a list.

title: Endpoint page
description: One endpoint as its readers see it: its row, the command or query it exposes, its handler, and its API requirements, each with its tests; and the endpoints of a command or query in a list.

title: Integration page
description: One integration as its readers see it: its row, its adapter and its tests; and the integrations of a product in a list.

title: UI component page
description: One UI component as its readers see it: its row, the views it renders, the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses; and the UI components of a product in a list.

title: Business outcome
description: One business outcome as its page reads it: its statement, measure and target, the tests and records that measure it, and the capabilities that serve it.

title: Test data set
description: A test data set as its readers read it: the Test data set page reads it whole with the tests that start from it; a domain's list reads each set's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Table
description: A table as its readers read it: the Table page reads it whole (the entity, read model or domain it sits under, its keys in order, the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses); the list under an entity, a read model or a domain reads each table's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Extension record
description: One record of a product's own kind as its page reads it: its kind and the kind's label, the record it sits under, its title and declared fields, the links it starts by relation and the packages it uses.

title: Entry point
description: One entry point whole: its row, the packages it uses and the standard rules it meets.

title: Tooling
description: One tooling record whole: its row, the packages it uses and the standard rules it meets.

title: Problems
description: The result of a run: every problem the checks found in the loaded data, each naming its check and record. Never stored; worked out on every load.

title: Check page
description: One check as its readers see it, Lathe's or a product's own; and the checks that run on a product, in run order.

title: Limits
description: A product's limits, its own or the defaults: the most children of one kind a record should hold and the most entities an aggregate should hold.

title: Space index
description: One index per space: the records of its product and of no product (SP01), their parts, the links among them, their coverage, and the space's problems with the workspace's.

title: Folder tree
description: Each product's nav tree: Shared, then each domain's five stages, the kind groups inside a stage that holds several kinds (SP03), and the records in them, placed by DS03.

title: Graph map
description: One map per product and layout: the folder tree (DS04) laid out once per load by DS05 (Tree) or DS07 (Nested), every node with its place, size and label.

title: ERD
description: A product's one ERD map: its domains, aggregates and entities as boxes and the lines between them, built once per data change, with the places they are laid out at, once per product and data change.

title: Record history
description: The commits that changed a record's rows, read from git on each request.

title: Spaces
description: Every product as a space in the rail, with its look and place.

title: Record changes
description: What changed in a product's records between a baseline and the data now, by record, computed on each ask.

title: Workspace
description: Every product's records, links, problems and coverage, as one load of the data files gives them: `Workspace` in `lathe/src/types.ts`. Filled from the data files whenever they change.

title: Keymap
description: Every keyboard command with its bindings as the platform shows them, which every hint, the palette and the sheet read.

title: Themes
description: Every theme, which one is in use and the color mode.

title: Recent folders
description: The recent folders, latest first, as File › Open Recent and the Dock menu list them.

title: Claude Code sessions
description: A folder's saved Claude Code sessions, from the CLI's own session store, each with its title, when it was last written, and whether another Claude client may have it open.

title: Reader's view
description: What a window shows the Reader: its page, the focused record, the stage, the record selected on the stage or in the wiki card, and whether the wiki card is open.

title: Coverage
description: Per domain and obligation kind: how many obligations are designed, built, proved and not automated yet, out of the total; and per obligation, the tests that count as its proof there.

title: Coverage gaps
description: Each obligation not designed, built or proved, with what it lacks.

title: Tests by state
description: Each domain's tests by state: automated, manual and not automated yet.

title: Owed pattern rules
description: Each pattern rule each following domain owes, with its standing there.

title: File facts
description: Each test and technical record that names a file: whether the file exists, and whether a test's file names its ID. With them, each endpoint's and view's route and whether the files of what implements it name it, and each route the code serves.

title: Record trace
description: The records that design, build and prove one record, by group.

title: Table facts
description: Each part a table kept in a database should have in the file it names (the table, each column, each primary, unique and foreign key), and whether that file defines it.

title: Following page
description: One following as its readers see it: the value, or the reason it does not apply, its follower gives each setting of its pattern; and the patterns a domain or use case follows.
